correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 44–90. On the short-period antipodal fiber through y=b/2 relative to the first site, radii below b/2 leave one arc shorter than a. For b/2<=r<R<=a/2, covering implies sqrt(r^2-b^2/4)+r>=a/2, equivalently r>=R in that range. For half-period sites the two horizontal widths at y in [0,b/2] sum to at least R+h=a/2 by concavity, strictly more inside, and the horizontal arc centers are antipodes. This verifies both cover and exclusion of interior fibers from the deepest holes. At R equality in the fiber measure bound forces the second site to y=b/2. For a>b the two proper arcs with total length a must tile, with antipodal midpoints; at a=b one of the arcs is the whole fiber, so horizontal uniqueness instead follows by testing (a/2,epsilon) and taking epsilon to zero. The endpoint fibers give exactly the stated contacts, including the collapse to two distinct torus points in the square case. Verified the one-center transition, the density normalization, the sign of the shape derivative, and the triangular basis at a/b=sqrt(3) (basis lengths b and angle 60 degrees). The multiplicity-counted lift density is not a torus-ball area ratio. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and checker.py lines 19–59 without running the frozen script: its 9,801 exact grid evaluations include periodic endpoint repeats and only test the proposed arrangement, not optimality or continuum exhaustiveness. The universal verification is the analytic fiber argument.
